target_customer: Homeowners and small businesses wanting live electricity readings, later landlords and submetering users via hardware partners
problem: People could not see how much electricity they were using in real time, so they could not connect behavior to the bill.
business_model: Hardware sensor sale plus tiered web subscription, later software on partner hardware

founders.name: Savraj Singh
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him under former founders as YC S07 and W09 alumnus, now at bubblegoods.com. TechCrunch Dec 2009 calls him co-founder but names no other. Education and prior employers not found in opened sources.

competitors.name: The Energy Detective (TED)
competitors.what: Current probe monitor for the electric panel with in-home display
competitors.traction_then: Described as too complicated for average consumers, priced about $145

competitors.name: Google PowerMeter
competitors.what: Web dashboard for home electricity use, announced February 2009, dependent on utility smart meters

competitors.name: Tendril
competitors.what: Boulder startup building a bridge between home displays and Itron meter networks
competitors.traction_then: Had pitched federal officials alongside Google and GE

technical_complexity.rationale: A sensor that reads a digital meter without an electrician plus a near real time web service updating about every 10 seconds, a hardware and web combination for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Competitors already sold monitors and Google and Microsoft were entering with free software, so little prevented copying; the main edge was working with existing meters.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google PowerMeter and Microsoft Hohm entered the space and both were later discontinued, per 2011 coverage found in search; neither bought Wattvision.

market_need_then: Rising interest in energy feedback in 2009 shown by the Google PowerMeter announcement and a wave of consumer monitors, though TED cost only about $145 as a one-time purchase.

branding.domain_note: Company site is wattvision.com, the exact .com, in use per its own page; acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found no press, brand pages or community evidence for this brand, so it is rated as the lowest tier by default, not as a judged weakness.

pivots.from: Selling a complete sensor plus software solution
pivots.to: Software that works with hardware partners (EKM and Rainforest gateways)
pivots.why: YC page says the company moved to software with hardware partners; own site notes EKM partnership since 2010.

outcome_analysis: Wattvision launched a WiFi sensor and web dashboard in late 2009 after YC W09 and ran a 2012 Kickstarter for a second sensor. It stayed small, with only a YC seed and crowdfunding found, then moved to software on partner hardware. The YC directory marks it inactive, yet its own site was live in 2026 selling tenant billing, so it looks like a small bootstrapped product more than a venture outcome; no cause of any shutdown is public.
notes: YC directory says Inactive but the company website was live in 2026, so the status may be stale; exit left unknown. The 2009 seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, $20K, Jan 26 2009); Seedtable gives Jan 2009 with no amount. StartupHub reports $67K total including crowdfunding, unverified. The Kickstarter round amount is unknown: a Techli snippet shows early pledges only, final total not confirmed. Microsoft Hohm named as competitor by TechCrunch Dec 2009 is too late for as_of. CB Insights page lists the company as acquired with no acquirer, unverified. Alexis Ohanian appears on a cap-table site as investor, unverified. Search found no shutdown cause.
